blindSummary:
This state/province holds a dedicated regional law on the right to identity and gender expression (in force since April 2017) alongside a general LGBTI-protection statute (2018), making it one of only three regions in the country to have enacted legislation in both the trans-specific and general-LGBTI-equality categories. Unlike one of the other two, this region has not amended or narrowed its provisions. The statutory framework supports institutional response channels for a visitor encountering discrimination.

No incident data, enforcement action, or negative visitor-facing finding was located for this region in the research pass. The regional capital carries a visible and well-established LGBTQ community with dedicated infrastructure. The difference from the national picture rests on the statutory-completeness evidence.

Of the three dual-category regions, this one's framework is active and unrevised: one peer region rolled its provisions back in 2023, and where regions have no such laws at all the difference turns entirely on the presence versus absence of statutory infrastructure.
blindSourceSummaries: Trans-rights federation's regional-legislation inventory: lists this state/province's two regional statutes - an integral law recognising the right to gender identity and expression (April 2017) and an LGBTI-equality law (December 2018) - and shows two peer regions as the only others holding both a trans-specific and a general LGBTI law (one pairing 2014 and 2017 statutes, the other two 2016 statutes); the basis for the dual-category claim in the summary.

LGBTI federation's 2025 review of public-education policies across the country's regions: tracks which regions have gender-identity protocols and education legislation; notes this region's parliament completing its gender legislation and groups it with four peer regions among the broadest in educational-policy coverage.
blindLocalsOnly: The regional identity-and-expression law's registry and administrative procedures operate for residents; a visitor never invokes them.
